findings.title: validate_connection logs raw httpx exception instead of a sanitized summary
findings.problem: User CLAUDE.md (absolute Security section): 'Never log sensitive data (passwords, tokens, PII, auth headers).' User CLAUDE.md precedence rule: 'before introducing a new pattern, check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that.' Project CLAUDE.md Deep Code Review Convention #1: 'No API keys in logs, responses, or HTML.' This diff replaces the previously safe `status=exc.response.status_code` field with `exc=exc`, logging `str(httpx.HTTPStatusError)` directly. The codebase already solves 'log exception detail safely' a different way: `triggarr/search/engine.py` defines `_sanitize_exc(exc)` ('Avoids storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink') and it is applied at ~25 call sites across engine.py/scheduler.py/routes.py. ROADMAP.md backlog item 999.6(a) explicitly flags the sibling file `triggarr/clients/sonarr.py:~49` for doing exactly this same thing ('logs httpx.HTTPError via logger.warning(exc=exc) WITHOUT _sanitize_exc; on legacy Sonarr installs the apikey rides in the request URL embedded in the exception... _sanitize_exc is applied consistently elsewhere; apply it here') as an unresolved, still-open BACKLOG item. This diff adds a second, near-identical instance of that same flagged anti-pattern into the shared `ArrClient` base class used by Radarr/Sonarr/Lidarr, rather than fixing it.
findings.current_code:
logger.warning(
    "{app}: Unexpected HTTP error: {exc}",
    app=self._app_name,
    exc=exc,
)
findings.fix_hint: Extract a safe summary instead of the raw exception object (mirror _sanitize_exc's HTTPStatusError branch, e.g. f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"); clients/base.py can't import _sanitize_exc directly without a circular import (search/engine.py imports triggarr.clients.radarr/sonarr/lidarr, which import clients.base), so inline the equivalent safe extraction locally, as this file did before the diff.
findings.why_it_matters: Under the current implementation the API key is sent via the X-Api-Key header (base.py:31-34), so this specific call path doesn't demonstrably leak it today -- but that's exactly the fragile assumption _sanitize_exc exists to not depend on, and the backlog already documents a legacy-URL-apikey scenario for the same client family. Logging the raw exception also defeats the redacting sink's reliability (it depends on exact substring match against known secrets) and removes the deliberate, already-safe pattern this very file used before the change.

members.title: Revert of security fix reintroduces API-key leak risk via raw httpx exception logging
members.problem: This hunk is a byte-for-byte revert of commit d47b4c2 ("fix(security): prevent potential key leakage in validate_connection log messages"), which deliberately replaced logging the raw httpx.HTTPStatusError with logging only exc.response.status_code. The diff reverts that fix, logging the full exception object again. str(httpx.HTTPStatusError) renders the request URL (`for url '...'`). Elsewhere in this exact codebase (triggarr/search/engine.py `_sanitize_exc`, triggarr/search/scheduler.py `_on_job_error`, triggarr/web/routes.py search_now/refresh_counts), the team explicitly documents that httpx exceptions 'may carry ?apikey= query strings on legacy *arr installs' and built a dedicated sanitizer specifically because raw str(exc) for httpx/pydantic exceptions 'may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink.' This diff reintroduces exactly the unsafe pattern that sanitizer was created to eliminate, in the one client file that previously had its own ad hoc safe formatting (status_code only) instead of _sanitize_exc.
members.why_it_matters: The loguru redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py) only strips exact, unmodified occurrences of known secret strings from the final formatted text. A URL-encoded, case-folded, or otherwise transformed copy of an API key embedded in an exception's rendered URL would not match and would reach stderr and the web UI log viewer buffer unredacted. This is precisely the scenario the original security fix (and the parallel _sanitize_exc mechanism used throughout engine.py/scheduler.py/routes.py) was built to close; reverting it here reopens that path in the one place it had already been fixed.
members.fix_hint: revert to logging exc.response.status_code (as before d47b4c2), or route through the existing triggarr.search.engine._sanitize_exc() helper so this call matches the sanitization convention used everywhere else in the codebase for httpx exceptions.

members.title: validate_connection now logs raw HTTPStatusError, bypassing the repo's established exception-sanitization pattern
members.problem: The diff changes the log value from `exc.response.status_code` to the raw `exc`. str(HTTPStatusError) includes the full request URL. The codebase already has an established way to handle this: `_sanitize_exc` in triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44 reduces HTTPStatusError to `HTTP {status_code}`. It is used at more than 20 call sites, including engine.py:366/420/487/619/881/1138, scheduler.py:228/362/387/407 and routes.py:968/1073. The same file follows the pattern inline at base.py:71-75 (`_request_with_retry`), and so does tracking.py:70-71. This hunk is the only place in the clients layer that logs a raw HTTPStatusError.
members.why_it_matters: The sanitization exists because str(exc) can carry the request URL (scheduler.py:401 documents stripping 'request.url credentials') past the loguru redacting sink. Logging the raw exception in one place breaks a guarantee the rest of the repo keeps on purpose, and future readers will copy the inconsistency.

members.title: Logging the raw HTTPStatusError can leak URL credentials into logs (sanitization removed)
members.problem: The old code logged only `exc.response.status_code`. The new code logs `exc=exc`, so loguru calls `str(HTTPStatusError)`. httpx builds that string as "... '<status>' for url '<full request.url>'\nFor more information check: ...", which puts the whole request URL, including base_url, into the log message. The rest of the codebase sends httpx exceptions through `_sanitize_exc` (triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44, which returns just `HTTP {status}`) for exactly this reason. Both triggarr/search/scheduler.py:218-224 and :400-403 say raw httpx exception text can carry `request.url` credentials. The redacting sink only removes the secret values it was given. config.py:74-75 still allows other query credentials such as `?token=foo`, and URL userinfo (`http://user:pass@host`) is not obviously in that list. Those values now reach stderr and the in-memory log buffer that the web UI shows. The same edit also drops the plain status-code summary used everywhere else in this file (compare the retry warning at base.py:71-75). pending: confirm whether collect_secrets (startup.py:78) includes URL userinfo or query tokens; if it does, only the non-apikey query-param leak remains.
members.why_it_matters: This removes the established log-sanitization control on a path that every connection check runs. Credentials kept in the configured URL can end up in plaintext logs and in the UI log viewer.
members.fix_hint: log `_sanitize_exc(exc)` or `exc.response.status_code`, as the rest of the codebase does

members.title: Credential exposure in logs: raw HTTPStatusError text (full request URL) now logged, bypassing the _sanitize_exc convention
members.problem: The non-401 branch of validate_connection used to log only `exc.response.status_code`. It now logs `exc` itself. str(httpx.HTTPStatusError) includes the full request URL, built from the configured base_url. Everywhere else the codebase deliberately avoids this. triggarr/search/engine.py:30-44 (_sanitize_exc) exists to 'avoid storing raw str(exc) which may contain internal paths, URLs, or API keys that bypass the loguru redacting sink'. scheduler.py:218-224/400-409 and routes.py:957-970/1063-1075 route every httpx/pydantic exception through it. base.py:71-75 (_request_with_retry) also logs only `HTTP {status}`. The redacting sink (triggarr/logging.py:36-41, 72-76) only replaces exact secret strings from collect_secrets (startup.py:78-95): the *arr API keys and auth secrets. Two concrete inputs get through that the old code never logged. (1) The URL validator explicitly allows non-apikey query credentials such as `?token=foo` for reverse-proxy setups (models/config.py:74-75). Those values are not in the secrets list, so a 403/404/5xx from system/status writes them verbatim to stderr and to the web UI log buffer. (2) Userinfo in base_url (`http://user:pass@host`) is also not a collected secret and would appear in the URL text. Every enabled *arr instance reaches this path at startup (startup.py:160). Any instance returning a non-401 error (for example a reverse proxy returning 403 or 502) triggers it.
members.why_it_matters: Proxy tokens or basic-auth credentials in the configured URL end up in container logs and the authenticated web log viewer. This reverses a sanitization convention the project applies everywhere else.
members.fix_hint: Revert to status-code-only logging, or use _sanitize_exc(exc) / f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}" to match base.py:71-75 and the CR-01 convention.

findings.title: Raw validation errors disclose sensitive response contents
findings.problem: A 200 response containing {"password":"upstream-private-secret"} without version reaches SystemStatus.model_validate at line 218. Verified that its ValidationError includes the password in input_value; this change now logs it. The previous error-count message excluded response contents. collect_secrets (startup.py:74–99) collects only configured API/auth secrets, and both logging sinks perform literal replacement (logging.py:36–40,72–76), so unrelated upstream credentials survive into stderr and the web log buffer. A misrouted or malformed upstream response can therefore disclose sensitive data.

findings.fix_hint: Restore count-only logging or emit allowlisted validation metadata without input values or context. Add a regression test asserting that sensitive fields in malformed responses never reach either logging sink.

members.title: Revert of security fix reintroduces verbose response-payload exposure via raw pydantic ValidationError logging
members.problem: This hunk reverts the second half of commit d47b4c2, which replaced logging the raw pydantic.ValidationError with logging only exc.error_count(). str(pydantic.ValidationError) embeds, per failing field, the raw 'input_value' that failed validation -- i.e. the actual *arr API response payload content -- rather than a safe summary. The same codebase's own _sanitize_exc() (triggarr/search/engine.py) deliberately reduces pydantic.ValidationError to "validation error ({count} issues)" for this reason, and that pattern is used consistently in scheduler.py and routes.py. This diff reintroduces the unsanitized form in base.py specifically.
members.why_it_matters: Dumping the full validation error exposes raw upstream API response content into logs and the redacted-log web viewer beyond what the redacting sink can filter (it only matches known secret literals, not arbitrary response structure), increasing the server-side log's information-disclosure surface and diverging from the project's established sanitization convention for this exact exception type.
members.fix_hint: revert to logging exc.error_count() (as before d47b4c2), or route through _sanitize_exc() for consistency with engine.py/scheduler.py/routes.py.

members.title: Logging the raw pydantic ValidationError puts untrusted response content into logs (sanitization removed)
members.problem: The old code logged only `exc.error_count()`. The new code logs `exc=exc`, and `str(pydantic.ValidationError)` includes `input_value=...` reprs of the failing response data. The configured URL can point at anything that answers on it, such as a reverse proxy, a login page or a misconfigured host. Its response body, which can be up to the pydantic truncation length per error and can include tokens, HTML or internal paths, now goes into the logs. This bypasses the codebase rule that pydantic exceptions go through `_sanitize_exc` (engine.py:42-43 returns `validation error (N issues)`; scheduler.py:231 and :408 apply it). pending: confirm what the SystemStatus endpoint can return through the configured proxies.

members.title: Upstream data exposure in logs: raw pydantic ValidationError text (input_value excerpts of the *arr response) now logged instead of error count
members.problem: The ValidationError branch used to log `exc.error_count()`. It now logs `exc`, whose str() is multi-line and embeds `input_value=...` excerpts of the upstream /system/status JSON for each failing field. When the endpoint returns an unexpected body (an HTML login page from an SSO/reverse proxy, or a different app on the port), that content goes verbatim into stderr and the web UI log buffer (logging.py:72-82). The redacting sink only strips exact configured secrets. This is the same class of output that _sanitize_exc (engine.py:42-43) reduces to `validation error (N issues)` for every other pydantic error in the codebase. The repo's CLAUDE.md also says not to expose internal error details. Impact is bounded: system/status itself is unlikely to carry the *arr API key, and the viewer requires auth.
members.why_it_matters: This loosens a deliberate logging control. Arbitrary upstream response content now reaches persisted logs and the UI log viewer, and multi-line output degrades the single-line log format.
members.fix_hint: Keep the error-count message (or use _sanitize_exc). If more diagnostics are wanted, log field locations only (e['loc'] for e in exc.errors()) without input values.
